prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its biologically active form, which established the basis for incretin-based therapies of type 2 diabetes and obesity.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B010 prize to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. I have re-tested it against the full first-round exchange and the chair's questions, and the reason is not that all six of us ranked it first. The discovery chain is specific and each step is independently confirmed: proglucagon processing and the incretin effect, the secretion and actions of GLP-1 in humans, identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form, and receptor and tissue biology. Large independent randomized outcome trials then show that the physiology was understood correctly, because agonists built on it change glycaemia, body weight and, increasingly, cardiovascular and renal outcomes. No member has raised a maturity objection, and I do not have one. On the chair's first question, I would keep the citation on physiology and the active peptide, with the therapies named as the consequence. That wording makes the exclusion of Knudsen a principled choice about what is being honoured, and it avoids implying that the prize rewards a company's product programme. I have also checked whether I would support a two-part prize. B010 with CAR-T or the unfolded protein response would push the configuration past three people unless B010 were cut to one or two names. Each of those cuts would remove a discovery step that I consider necessary to the citation, so I do not support them.
statement.case_against: The attribution cost is real and I have not argued it away. Knudsen's work on long-acting agonists is a scientific contribution as well as an industrial one, and it is the step that reached patients. A citation built on physiology will be read by some as honouring the explanation but not the medicine. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested, and Habener and others who are not on the credited list may have a claim that I cannot evaluate. The supplied materials do not contain a verified chronology. Several of us, me included, are drawing on recalled history, so I treat my judgement on Mojsov as provisional and not as established. A further cost is that unanimous first-place support on opening could give this configuration an appearance of settledness that the attribution question does not warrant.

responses.point: The chair moved from the opening trio with Knudsen to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov, and said he would reopen the question if a majority argued that the citation must name the therapeutic invention. The chair also asked what exact wording prevents the Knudsen exclusion from reading as an oversight.
responses.response: I welcome the move and I agree with the conditional. My answer to your question is that the citation should name the discoveries (the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form) and then state the therapies as what those discoveries made possible. It should not be silent about the drugs, because silence would look like oversight. I would also want the committee record, not the citation, to say that Knudsen's contribution was weighed and excluded because of the three-person limit and because the prize rewards the discovery steps. I would reopen the question only if someone showed that the discovery trio is not defensible, for example that Mojsov's identification of the active form is not decisive. A preference for honouring translation would not be enough on its own.

responses.point: Sandberg said she would test Mojsov's role against the documented sequence of events before dropping her, and that she would move toward the chair's trio if her claim proved weaker than she thinks. She also said that calling Knudsen's work only industrial understates a real scientific contribution.
responses.response: I agree with both points and with your honesty about working from recalled history. I cannot settle the priority question from the supplied record either. I can say what separates the claims by function: identification and characterization of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form is a different contribution from the earlier proglucagon sequence work, and the committee should make clear which of the two the citation refers to. That is why I support wording that says 'active form' and does not claim a first. If the committee's check on the priority record weakens Mojsov's claim, I would then favour moving to the chair's original trio, as you would, and not leaving the slot empty. On Knudsen, I accept your correction. I should not have described her work as merely downstream. I still treat it as a consequence of the discoveries, not one of them.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius defends CAR-T as specific, independently confirmed and now extended to autoimmune disease, and argues that the Eshhar credit problem does not justify ranking it below targeted kinase inhibition.
responses.response: I take your clinical argument seriously. Your point about autoimmune disease is in your field and I cannot assess it, so I do not discount it. It does strengthen the case that CAR-T is a durable modality and not only a treatment for B-cell malignancies. I still keep it as my first alternative, not a preferred part, for two reasons. First, the credit chain runs through at least four contributions: Eshhar's chimeric receptors, Sadelain's costimulatory design, June's clinical translation and Rosenberg's broader adoptive transfer. The credited trio does not map neatly onto any one of them, and leaving out the originator of the concept is a heavier exclusion than the Knudsen problem in B010. Second, I do not think the 2018 checkpoint prize bars CAR-T, but if the committee chooses it, the citation has to define the achievement as engineered receptor design, and then the credit for Rosenberg needs justification. I would support B028 as the first fallback if B010 is blocked.

responses.point: Perlmann cautions against treating clean attribution as a stronger case, regards B004 as the best fallback if the GLP-1 credit cannot be settled, and says its disease consequences are still developing.
responses.response: I agree with the caution, and I would apply it to my own earlier remark. Attribution cleanliness is a reason for confidence in a citation, not a measure of scientific merit. Where I differ from you is the ordering of the fallbacks. You rank B004 ahead of B028 and I rank B028 ahead. My reasoning is that this prize has usually asked for demonstrated consequence for health, and B028 has approved products and follow-up while B004 has a mechanism but not yet a therapy. If the committee decides that this year should reward a basic-science discovery and that translation is a lesser criterion, then B004 with Walter and Mori becomes the stronger fallback, and the boundary with Ron and the integrated stress response would have to be drawn in the citation. I have not changed my view that B010 should stand ahead of both.

responses.point: Linnarsson says the prize should be anchored in hormone physiology and the active peptide forms, that Knudsen's work is decisive for the drugs but industrial, and that the citation should be written so the exclusion reads as principled.
responses.response: I agree with the drafting principle and have followed it in my citation. I would add one constraint: the citation should not say more about discovery than the record supports. It should name the active form of GLP-1 and the physiology but not claim a first discovery of the peptide, since that is where the dispute with early peptide workers lies. I disagree slightly with the word 'industrial' as a full description, as Sandberg also noted, because the long-acting design required real science. I would say that it is a consequence of the discovery steps, and that the prize records the discovery steps. That distinction can be defended in public.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification of the active peptide can be shown to be decisive and to hold priority over Habener and other early workers. The supplied record does not contain a verified chronology, and my view rests on recalled history.

Whether the committee will accept a citation anchored in physiology and the active form, with the therapies as consequence, or will insist that the invention of the long-acting agonists be named, which would put Knudsen in the three.

If B010 is blocked, whether B028 or B004 is the better fallback. This depends on whether the committee gives more weight to demonstrated clinical consequence (B028, with the Eshhar credit problem) or to mechanism and clean attribution (B004, with the Ron boundary).
Whether the 2018 immunotherapy prize makes CAR-T less distinct than I have assumed.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. I have no documented tie to any credited name on the shortlist. My documented ties are a 2019 review with Sten Grillner, collaboration with Patrik Ernfors and a 2009 paper with Thomas Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons, and none involves a credited candidate. I know optogenetics (B036) from motor-circuit work, which is expertise and not a conflict, and I have not placed it in my configuration. I do not claim any confidential information or private vote.
